summary.intent: Keep a multi-PR release pipeline moving: fix a misleading CI check name, resolve a merge conflict in PR #604 (change #212), then work through the post-merge backlog toward the 0.22.0 release.
summary.outcome: Fixed the CI check name in #607 and resolved the #604 conflict (merge commit 441b620). All PRs were then merged and release PR #558 is ready. Follow-up sessions were launched for the dry-run and flaky-test fixes, and the homepage-key cleanup is in progress.

repo: A job-level `if: github.event_name == 'push'` skips the job before matrix expansion, so on PRs GitHub shows the raw name `Release Artifact Preflight (${{ matrix.id }})`. Fix: give the skipped job a static name.
The macOS and Linux preflight jobs shared the same name string, so a blanket sed renamed both. The Linux job always runs and expands correctly, so it must keep its matrix name.
No required status check depended on the preflight job name, so the label bug never blocked merges.
#604 removed `build_release_intent_with_artifacts` and changed `build_release_intent`'s signature. #603 added `ValidatedReleaseIntent`. Both changes had to be kept in the CLI import list.
CI validates `callisto.toml` with the released binary, so converting the repo's own config to `targets` must wait for 0.22.0.
`AGENTS.md` requires an in-progress migration to be finished or tracked, which is why the git-boundary call sites are slated for completion.
Redundant `homepage` keys cause cargo to warn on every build.
The process-count test flakes under load (10 vs 11 Git processes).
`version --dry-run` with a leftover checkpoint can report another directory's plan. The fix is to run the workspace checks before the permit gate.
workflow: Run `just workflow-contracts` after editing CI workflows to validate them.
Use worktrees (EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree) for isolated fixes and conflict merges.
After a broad sed, check for unintended matches, such as the Linux job that shared the name.
After resolving a conflict, compile, clippy and test the affected crates against the newly merged code, not only the conflict hunk.
Recommend a merge order so in-flight PRs that touch the same files don't keep conflicting.
Stop idle sessions and launch fresh follow-up sessions rather than leaving them running.
Triage the backlog with a 'worth it, simplest version' check: fix wrong-output bugs and flakes, defer items that need design.

friction: The CI check name bug introduced by #593 confused the user.
A second merge conflict appeared in #604 after main moved again, frustrating the user.
The sed rename over-matched and changed the Linux preflight job, which then had to be restored.
The homepage-key removal command ran twice with no visible result in the transcript.
open_items: Merge release PR #558 (callisto 0.22.0). It is the first real run of the new pack, attest and publish workflows, so watch it closely.
After the release, convert the repo's own `callisto.toml` to `targets`.
Run the real-registry proof (R): tokenless publishing on npm and PyPI, plus onboarding time measured with new users. It needs the user's accounts.

Finish migrating Git call sites that still bypass the boundary, after follow-up session ca942951 (const-generic `LogEntry`, duplicate error closures, duplicate config tests) lands, since both touch `boundary.rs`.
Finish the dry-run checkpoint fix and the flaky process-count test fix, both launched as sessions.
Finish and land the homepage-key cleanup.
Design work still in the backlog: an extra cascade patch release, npm staged publishing, and publint.
